taxonomy:
Here is a taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games, based only on the rule descriptions you provided.

## 1) Loop-drawing puzzles
These puzzles require drawing one continuous loop through the grid, usually with cell- or dot-based constraints.

### 1.1 Simple single-loop with clue constraints
- **Slitherlink** — single loop around dots; numbers show how many lines surround a cell.
- **Numberlink** — connect identical numbered pairs with continuous lines; lines cannot cross or use numbered cells.
- **Yajilin** — single loop with black cells and arrow clues.
- **Mid-loop** — loop through cells; black circles must lie at the midpoint of a straight segment.
- **Suraromu** — loop with “gates” and a numbered starting circle.
- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop through all white circles, with straight/turn behavior constrained by enclosed areas.
- **Masyu** — loop through black and white circles with straight/turn requirements.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop through rooms, alternating moon-only and sun-only rooms.
- **Nagareru** — directed loop following arrow direction and wind constraints.

### 1.2 Loop puzzles with directional or movement rules
- **Nagareru**
- **Suraromu**
- **Yajilin**
- **Moon-or-Sun**

---

## 2) Region partitioning / tiling puzzles
These puzzles divide the grid into regions, blocks, rooms, or tiles with shape/size constraints.

### 2.1 Rectangular region puzzles
- **Shikaku** — divide the grid into rectangles, each with one number.
- **Heyawake** — rooms are predefined; paint cells with room-count and line-span constraints.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with numbers 1..n, plus arrow constraints.
- **Tilepaint** — tiles must be uniformly colored/uncolored; final shape outline emerges.
- **Choco Banana** — black and white areas must form matching pairs within a block.
- **Double Choco** — blocks contain matching white and gray regions of same shape.
- **Sto-stone** — rooms have black-cell counts; dropped stones must fill the lower half.
- **Usowan** — one wrong number per room; colored/uncolored cells with adjacency constraints.
- **Nuritwin** — each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks.
- **Nurimeizu** — rooms of paint/white, maze-style global constraints.
- **Juosan** — territories of horizontal/vertical marks with count constraints.

### 2.2 Shape-fitting / polyomino puzzles
- **LITS** — fill each area with a tetromino; no same-shaped tetrominoes touching except corners.
- **Evolomino** — blocks grow by adding one square without rotating/flipping.
- **Five Cells** — divide into 5-cell blocks.
- **Sashigane** — divide into one-cell-wide L-shaped blocks.
- **Shakashaka** — place black triangles so remaining white space forms rectangles/squares.
- **Nurimisaki** — white “promontory” cells form straight-line patterns and avoid 2×2+ groups.
- **Chained Block** — black-cell blocks must form a chain, with uniqueness of shape within a chain.

---

## 3) Number-placement puzzles
These puzzles focus on filling cells with numbers under structural constraints.

### 3.1 Complete numeric grids
- **Sudoku** — fill 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 blocks.
- **Fillomino** — partition board into size-matched numbered blocks.
- **Ripple Effect** — rooms contain consecutive numbers starting from 1; repeats in row/column must be spaced apart.
- **Nansuke** — fill blank cells with numbers from a list, vertically or horizontally.

### 3.2 Local number clues with area constraints
- **Kurodoko** — numbers indicate visible white-cell counts to nearest black cell/frame.
- **Kurotto** — circles give the sum of continuous black cells extending in four directions.
- **Makaro** — arrow clues point to the largest adjacent number in a room.
- **Hebi** — snake numbers 1 to 5 form ordered snake parts; black cells give directional visibility counts.
- **Usowan** — numbers count adjacent colored cells, with one wrong number per room.
- **Yosenabe** — gray-area sums equal the numbers of circles entering them.
- **Satogaeri** — circle movement lengths are given by numbers.
- **Shakashaka** — numbers count black triangles around them.
- **Dotchi-Loop** — white-circle behavior depends on area type, not pure numerals, but it is clue-based.
- **Nurimisaki** — circle numbers give straight-line length of white cells from a promontory.
- **Sashigane** — open circles/arrows are size and orientation clues.
- **Pencils** — pencil lengths are given by numbers in the pencil.
- **Juosan** — territory numbers constrain counts of horizontal/vertical marks.

---

## 4) Connectivity and separation puzzles
These involve connected white regions, disconnected black cells, or network continuity.

### 4.1 White-cell connectivity puzzles
- **Hitori** — black cells cannot touch; white cells must remain connected.
- **Kurodoko** — white cells must be connected; black cells cannot touch.
- **Nurikabe** — white islands and one continuous black wall; black 2×2 forbidden.
- **Heyawake** — white cells cannot stretch across more than two rooms and cannot be separated by painted cells.
- **Nurimisaki** — white cells must form a continuous network.
- **Usowan** — white cells must not be separated by colored cells.
- **Nurimeizu** — white cells must not be entirely cut off and must not form a loop.
- **LITS** — colored squares must form a connected network.

### 4.2 Black-cell connectivity / wall puzzles
- **Nurikabe**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Hitori**
- **Norinori** — blocks of two black squares in each region.
- **Sto-stone** — black cells in rooms, with gravity-style final arrangement.
- **Shakashaka** — black triangles carve out white rectangles/squares.

---

## 5) Pairing and matching puzzles
These puzzles emphasize matching identical items, pairs, or same shapes.

- **Hashiwokakero** — connect islands with bridges matching the island numbers.
- **Double Choco** — pair same-form white and gray areas.
- **Nuritwin** — exactly two equal-sized blocks per region.
- **Numberlink** — pair identical numbers with one continuous path.
- **Choco Banana** — matching white and gray shapes inside a block.
- **Evolomino** — blocks evolve by adding squares in sequence.
- **Satogaeri** — each country ends with one circle after movement.
- **Nansuke** — fill cells with numbers from a given list.
- **Yosenabe** — circles enter gray areas to match area sums.

---

## 6) Directional / arrow-based puzzles
These use arrows or directions as core constraints.

- **Hebi** — arrows on black cells show visibility direction.
- **Makaro** — arrows point to the largest adjacent number.
- **Sashigane** — arrows point toward the knee of an L-shaped block.
- **Suraromu** — gate-crossing order is constrained from a start circle.
- **Nagareru** — arrows define loop direction and wind.
- **Pencils** — pencil tips and line direction.
- **Satogaeri** — circles move by specified distances.
- **Yajilin** — arrows indicate black cells in a direction.
- **Yosenabe** — arrows show movement of circles into gray areas.
- **Shakashaka** — not arrow-based, but orientation-based via triangles.

---

## 7) Adjacency / spacing constraint puzzles
These puzzles enforce specific local spacing or touching rules.

- **Hitori** — duplicate numbers, no touching blacks.
- **Kurodoko** — black cells cannot touch.
- **Nurikabe** — black cells cannot form 2×2 or larger.
- **LITS** — colored squares cannot form 2×2 or larger.
- **Norinori** — each area contains exactly two black squares.
- **Usowan** — colored cells cannot touch; white connectivity required.
- **Nurimisaki** — no 2×2 or larger groups of either color.
- **Shakashaka** — remaining white cells must form rectangles/squares.
- **Chained Block** — blocks in a chain cannot duplicate shape.

---

## 8) Snake / path progression puzzles
These involve sequential progression through a set of cells.

- **Hebi** — snake numbers from 1 to 5 connected in order.
- **Evolomino** — blocks evolve by adding one cell at a time.
- **Pencils** — pencil lines extend from tips by given lengths.
- **Satogaeri** — circles move through tracks to countries.
- **Numberlink** — continuous paths linking pairs.
- **Masyu** — loop path constrained by circle types.
- **Mid-loop** — loop through black-circle midpoints.

---

## 9) Count-and-fill puzzles
These are dominated by numeric counts of neighboring, visible, or enclosed cells.

- **Akari** — bulbs illuminate cells; numbered cells count adjacent bulbs.
- **Kurodoko** — visible white-cell count to nearest black/frame.
- **Kurotto** — sum of black-cell runs around circles.
- **Shakashaka** — numbers count nearby triangles.
- **Usowan** — numbers count neighboring colored cells, with one wrong clue per room.
- **Hashiwokakero** — island number equals bridge count.
- **Norinori** — each room contains two black cells.
- **Fillomino** — block size equals number.
- **Five Cells** — blocks must have exactly five cells.
- **Ripple Effect** — consecutive numbers and spacing rules.
- **Sudoku** — each row/column/block contains 1–9.
- **Makaro** — arrow compares adjacent numbers.

---
